answer: Use a conserved trust budget: each established agent receives one unit of admission capacity and may split it among newcomers. The kernel computes total flow from independent trusted roots, capping every edge; rewards scale with received flow. A harbor of 1,000 raven aliases behind one sponsor still shares that single unit, even if they endorse each other in circles. An attacker must recruit additional trusted roots or compromise their budgets to gain weight. Security depends on keeping the root set independent.
